hymns:adoro-te.title: Adoro te devote
hymns:adoro-te.cut_by: recut 2026-09-26 (this build), from the 2026-09-15 line rows

licence_gate.rule: launch plan D4 / ADR 0001: public-domain editions or own work only

roman-missal-received.edition: received liturgical text (Roman Missal), as transcribed into the batch notes 2026-09-14/15
roman-missal-received.license_basis: 13th-century text; no modern critical edition used
roman-missal-received.open: Adoro te is not yet checked against a named PD printing; Pange lingua was checked against Britt 1922 and differs in orthography only (cenae/coenae, iubilatio/jubilatio, gentium/Gentium, Britt prints no Amen). Canonical orthography is Adam's call (Latin Hymns doc s.7, decision 2).

hopkins-1918.edition: Gerard Manley Hopkins, Poems, ed. Bridges (London, 1918)
hopkins-1918.open: Quoted from memory in the batch note; verify every stanza against the printed 1918 text before any public use.

caswall-1849-britt-1922.edition: Edward Caswall's translation (Lyra Catholica, 1849) as printed in Matthew Britt, The Hymns of the Breviary and Missal (1922), pp. 183-185, archive.org/details/hymnsofbreviarym00britrich
caswall-1849-britt-1922.open: Britt uses American spellings (honor, fulfills); Caswall's 1849 printing presumably differs. Canonical edition is Adam's call.

britt-1922-prose.what: Pange lingua: stanza-level literal prose (the PD candidate for `elegant`)
britt-1922-prose.edition: Matthew Britt, The Hymns of the Breviary and Missal (1922), literal prose per stanza

house-draft-2026-09-14.what: token gloss (wooden), lemma, parsing, syntax; teacher notes
house-draft-2026-09-14.edition: AK/Claude machine draft, Thomas Batch 01 (2026-09-14) and 02 (2026-09-15)
house-draft-2026-09-14.open: machine draft, unchecked by Adam. Since D3 its lemma and parsing are the fallback: each token's `provenance` says which source its value came from.

whitaker-words.what: token lemma (and parsing, where unambiguous): the Latin lemma spine, launch plan D3
whitaker-words.edition: WORDS 1.97F data (mk270 port), https://github.com/mk270/whitakers-words at 1f2f0fb0867a; analyses in data/lemmas/whitaker-la/hymns.analyses.jsonl (pipeline/README-lemma-spine.md)
whitaker-words.license_basis: Copyright William A. Whitaker (1936-2010), with an unconditional grant of any and all use of program and data. Not public domain.

evidence.what: the author's own documentation, WORDS 1.97F (sections 'Licence' and the program notice)

evidence.what: LICENCE.txt in the maintained port, at the pinned commit

whitaker-words.attribution: WORDS, a Latin dictionary, by Colonel William Whitaker (USAF, Retired)
whitaker-words.open: The grant is not the house's PD-or-own gate (launch plan D4 / ADR 0001). It is admitted here as its own class, `free-grant`, pending Adam's ruling. The grant asks, as a courtesy, 'at least tell me'; the author died in 2010.

house-retrofit-2026-09-15.what: prose_order, plain_form, absorbed (the plain column's four mechanisms)

house-elegant-2026-09-15.license_basis: the batch file records this as PD; it is the house's own prose, recorded here as own

house-recut-2026-09-26.what: the clause cut of Adoro te; concatenated prose_order for joined lines
house-recut-2026-09-26.open: unchecked by Adam; five joins, each with its grammatical reason in `cut.why`.

token_fields.surface: the reading of record, exactly as transcribed
token_fields.translit: null by rule on a Latin-script witness; filled only for grc/he
token_fields.lemma: whitaker-words where its headword is the draft's and one entry is picked out; else house-draft-2026-09-14, flagged in `review`. Per token: provenance.lemma
token_fields.parsing: whitaker-words where it gives exactly one parse, the draft agrees and adds no teaching note; else house-draft-2026-09-14. Never invented. Per token: provenance.parsing
token_fields.lemma_key: whitaker-words: the WORDS dictionary form naming the lemma; null where the draft stands
token_fields.gloss: house-draft-2026-09-14: the wooden gloss, Latin order
token_fields.plain_form: house-retrofit-2026-09-15; null where the gloss serves as-is

perseus.policy: Perseus is CC BY-SA. Nothing from Perseus is in these files. Perseus enrichment (lemmata, morphology, treebank links) is a separate layer keyed by CTS URN and joined at read time, never merged in.
perseus.note: Neither hymn has a Perseus/CTS edition; the URN is null, not guessed.
